hero.title: Evidence of how Lowcountry Digital Works approaches real systems.
hero.lede: These examples distinguish what is live, what is in active development, and what exists only as internal service-enabling infrastructure. They are not presented as completed customer case studies.

projects.name: Lowcountry Digital Works website
projects.purpose: A public business site that demonstrates the same low-complexity, customer-owned, validation-first website practices LDW recommends.
projects.description: A lightweight Astro site with repository-controlled content, local brand assets, Cloudflare edge delivery, protected-main review, and browser/accessibility regression coverage.
evidence: Static-first Astro build with no CMS or database
Automated browser and accessibility regression checks
projects.boundary: The public site contains no customer portal, analytics SaaS, contact-form processor, or customer-data store.

projects.name: Document Control
projects.purpose: Explore structured document workflow, review, accountability, audit history, search, and export without claiming a completed customer deployment.
projects.description: A configurable LDW workflow application being developed service-first around controlled document lifecycle needs.
projects.boundary: Active development is not presented as a finished client engagement or mature standalone SaaS.

projects.name: Secure Exchange
projects.purpose: Develop a provider-neutral pattern for protected message and document exchange with clear queue ownership, retention, and accountability.
projects.description: Current foundation work uses a customer-owned isolated-deployment direction with an AWS-first reference architecture; production customer infrastructure is not yet provisioned.
evidence: Secure external intake and outbound workflow design
Individual workforce accountability and queue routing
Provider-neutral core with customer-owned deployment direction
projects.boundary: No public website claim implies that LDW currently operates production Secure Exchange infrastructure for customers.

projects.name: G.A.S. Engine
projects.purpose: Preserve normalized website-quality and visibility evidence so human-reviewed recommendations can be compared over time.
projects.description: G.A.S. is LDW-operated internal evidence and measurement infrastructure supporting managed-service validation. It is not customer SaaS, a standalone commercial product, or a self-service SEO platform.
evidence: Provider-neutral typed facts within accepted boundaries
Supports service-first Search + AI Visibility validation
projects.boundary: G.A.S. remains internal infrastructure; customer-facing service claims and pricing remain governed by the separate Managed Search + AI Visibility gate.

technology.title: Technology chosen in proportion to the problem.
technology.lede: These are examples of technologies currently used in LDW website, application, automation, and delivery work. A project does not inherit a platform simply because it appears here.

items.name: GitHub
items.description: Source control, review, and delivery workflows

items.name: Cloudflare
items.description: DNS, edge hosting, security, and deployment

technology.trademarkNote: Product names and marks are used only to identify technologies used in the work. Their owners do not sponsor or endorse Lowcountry Digital Works.

principle.title: The stack should serve the work, not become the work.
principle.body: A small static website, an offline tool, an automation, or a more involved workflow system can all be the right answer in different situations. The goal is to choose the simplest maintainable architecture that meets the actual requirements.
